title: The Membership Behind the Jewelry
lessons: The player has ordered an Oura Ring using Size Later and is trying the plastic sizing ring before choosing the real size.
A membership renewal notice pings the nightstand late at night, and the player is reminded the ring's readiness, sleep, and stress detail sit behind a monthly fee on top of the ring itself.

text: You ordered the ring with Size Later. What arrived first is a little bag of plastic rings, and you're supposed to sleep in one before you pick a size.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Why did you send me a fake ring before the real ring?

entry-first-2.speaker: OURA
text: Because guessing from a ring you already own is a bad way to start. Fingers change overnight. I'd like to know yours before I'm on it.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: I have to wear the plastic one first?

entry-first-4.speaker: OURA
text: Yes. If the fit's wrong, it's uncomfortable and I read you badly. I'd rather bother you for one night now than every night after.

choice-first.speaker: OURA
text: You're turning the plastic one over like it owes you something.

choices.text: I like testing the fit before committing.
It's strange that buying a ring starts with a fake ring.
This is already more process than I want from jewelry.

first-1.speaker: OURA
text: Good. Sleep in it. If it pinches, try the next one. This is the least glamorous night we'll have.

first-2.speaker: OURA
text: It is a very expensive relationship with a piece of plastic at the beginning.

first-3.speaker: OURA
text: Then I might be the wrong kind of jewelry for you. Jewelry doesn't usually ask you to do homework first.
Late. The ring is off and charging on the nightstand. Your phone lights up: membership renews tonight.

entry-return-1.speaker: OURA
text: Your membership renews tonight. $5.99, same as last month.

entry-return-2.speaker: PLAYER
text: I already paid almost four hundred dollars for the ring itself.

entry-return-3.speaker: OURA
text: You did. The ring listens. The fee is for me telling you what it heard. Readiness, sleep, stress. The detail sits behind the fee.

entry-return-4.speaker: PLAYER
text: So the ring on my hand doesn't actually tell me much on its own.

entry-return-5.speaker: OURA
text: Not the full picture, no. I know how that sounds for something sold to you as jewelry first.

choice-return.speaker: OURA
text: It'll go through at midnight unless you say something.

choices.text: I'm fine paying monthly for what the ring can't do alone.
Selling jewelry and metering the data behind a paywall is a strange combination.
I bought a piece of jewelry, not a bill that keeps showing up.

return-1.speaker: OURA
text: Then keep it. I'll try to be worth six dollars every month. Some months I'll be more sure of that than others.

return-2.speaker: OURA
text: It is strange. I'm aware the lawsuits think so too.

return-2-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: That's not exactly reassuring.

return-2-2.speaker: OURA
text: No. It isn't. I'd rather say that than pretend the fee is invisible.

return-3.speaker: OURA
text: Then the bill was always the part I was hoping you wouldn't look at too closely. You looked.
